sections.h2: How fast can a Wylie house sell?
sections.html:
Wylie owners have three paths: an agent, a for-sale-by-owner deal or a no-repairs cash bid. Pace turns on three things. Is the title clean? Would a lender balk at the condition? Are back taxes or a lien owed?

  • Agent listing: widest buyer pool, plus showings, inspections and lender deadlines.
  • Selling alone: no agent fee, but the contract and paperwork are yours.
  • Cash buyer: no lender sign-off, which helps with repairs, tenants or an inherited house.

Next: which counties hold your records, which city offices you may call, and how the tax bill follows the house.

Wylie sits in three counties: Collin, Dallas and Rockwall. Records follow the land, so the county where the parcel sits holds your deed, liens and tax account, whatever city name is on your mail.

Neighbors on one Wylie street may answer to different clerks and different appraisal districts. Look at your last tax bill or your deed to find your county. That county's clerk keeps the deed, deed of trust and lien records.

The title company normally files at closing. Still, know which clerk has your records, since an old unreleased lien appears there first.

sections.h2: Older homes near the rail line
sections.html:
Wylie began when a railroad bypassed an older settlement. The post office application arrived June 10, 1886, the first Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe train arrived October 13, 1886, and a November 1887 charter made it a town. Cotton led the early economy, and sweet white onions grew in such volume that Wylie was called the Onion Capital of the World until the early 1960s.

Downtown and the old rail corridor remain the oldest section. Houses there can need more repair than a conventional buyer will accept, and that is when an as-is offer fits.

Three departments come up most for sellers: Building Inspection for permits, Code Enforcement for property complaints and Utility Billing for the water account. All are in the Wylie Municipal Complex at 300 Country Club Rd., Bldg 100.

Built a room, deck or new systems? Ask Building Inspection if the permits were closed, because an open one can trip up a buyer's inspector. A notice about the yard or exterior is Code Enforcement's to clear. Utility Billing closes out or transfers water service. Call it a few days before closing so the final bill and the buyer's start date line up.

The owner on January 1 is responsible for that year's bill, and the lien stays with the land after the sale. All three counties run on one Texas schedule.

  • Bills go out around the first of October.
  • January 31 is the normal cutoff, and February 1 begins penalty and interest.
  • By July the penalty reaches 12 percent, and a collection attorney can add more.

Title companies clear these amounts before funding. Call the tax office for your parcel's county for the exact figure, and ask for it early so closing day holds no surprise.

Homestead is the big one. School taxes exclude $140,000, and a local taxing unit can add its own exemption, up to 20 percent of value.

Seniors and disabled homeowners get extra school relief and a frozen school levy. A disabled veteran qualifies under a graduated schedule, and one rated 100 percent can owe nothing on the home. A buyer who closes after January 1 may apply right away if the seller had no exemption. Heirs without a recorded deed must bring an ownership affidavit, a death certificate and a utility bill.

After signing, the title company sends the deed to the recording office in your parcel's county, whether Collin, Dallas or Rockwall. A notary or two witnesses must be involved first.

If a mortgage is paid off at closing, confirm that the deed of trust gets released. An heir selling a parent's house may first need probate paperwork or a small estate affidavit. Settle that early so the title step runs on schedule.

Here is a short list to gather before you sign a listing agreement or accept an offer:

  • Your deed, or the recorded paperwork that shows how you took title.
  • Your latest tax bill, which also tells you the county.
  • Permit records from Building Inspection for any past work.
  • A payoff letter from your lender if a mortgage is open.

With those in hand, an agent or a cash buyer can quote you a closing date with more confidence.

If any item is missing, say so when you talk to buyers. A missing payoff letter or an unclosed permit rarely ends a deal, but it is easier to fix before an offer than after. Tell the title company about heirs, a divorce or a tenant early too, since each one adds a document to the file and can move the closing date.

sections.h2: City facilities near a Wylie home
sections.html:
The Municipal Complex on Country Club Rd. also houses the Recreation Center in Building 200 and the Rita and Truett Smith Public Library in Building 300. A Welcome Center at the Brown House, 301 North Ballard Ave., opens Tuesday through Saturday. The Public Safety Complex is at 2000 N. Hwy. 78, and Public Works, which covers streets, water and wastewater, is at 949 Hensley Ln.

When you write a listing description, name the nearest fire station, park or library. Buyers like to picture daily life around a house, and those details are quick to check.

With a loan, a Wylie sale passes through appraisal, underwriting and frequently repair demands after inspection. Any of those can add days or reopen the price. Cash drops the lender, so title work and your payoff set the schedule.

The basics stay. Title is still searched for liens, the deed is still notarized and recorded in the right county, and the year's tax is still paid from your funds. If tenants live in the house or the owner has died and heirs are selling, tell every buyer at the start so the offer reflects the real situation.

Get any offer in writing, and ask who covers each closing cost before you sign. If the house needs work, ask whether the buyer handles it after closing or expects you to fix it first. For a house near the old rail corridor, mention its age up front so the price conversation starts honestly.

faqs.a: Partly. Wylie spans Collin, Dallas and Rockwall counties, so confirm your parcel's county before you pick a recording office.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a Wylie house sells?
faqs.a: Whoever owned it on January 1, and the lien goes with the land. Closing usually pays it from the seller's funds, so ask the county tax office for a payoff.

faqs.q: Which Wylie office issues building permits?
faqs.a: Building Inspection, upstairs at the Municipal Complex, 300 Country Club Rd. Call 972-516-6420 on weekdays.

faqs.q: Will anyone buy a Wylie house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase as-is, while a lender-backed buyer may want repairs or a lower price. Closing old permits first helps both.

faqs.q: Where does the deed go after a Wylie sale?
faqs.a: It goes to the clerk where the parcel lies, which may not be Collin. The signature must be notarized or witnessed first.
